intro: Biggest rank disagreements between the SEI board and SP+, 2026 season: from the SP+ top 15 and from our own top 15.

teams.explanation: SP+ sits at #50 because the scoreboard says middle-class: +49 margin, #30 nationally, with a 23-29 loss at Indiana dragging the average. SEI reads the plays instead. The Wildcats turn drives into touchdowns at an elite clip (TD% +2.03 SD, red-zone TD% +1.90) and they did it at home against Penn State, 34-13, while forcing takeaways at a strong rate (INT% +1.79). The one feature SP+ seems to price hard is discipline — penalty z -1.86. Process over results, exactly where the two boards split.
hints: Process outran scoreboard: margin rank #30 (margin +49) but SEI #3.
SP+ halves: off #59, def #34.
Strongest metrics: TD% +2.03, RZ TD% +1.90, INT% +1.79.
Weakest metrics: Pen -1.86.

teams.explanation: SP+ sits at #53; SEI says #15. The 2-2 FBS record (a 24-27 opening loss to SMU, then 36-50 at Alabama) keeps the scoreboard view mediocre — margin #43 — but SP+ is harsher still, pricing their defense at #74. The play-level picture splits: the offense is genuinely good (red-zone TD% +1.72, 2nd-down PPA +1.71, our off #10), while the defense is merely average on our board (def #41) and the penalty chart is ugly (-1.72 yards per play conceded on fouls). SP+'s read is mostly the losses; ours is that the Seminoles played two games where the process was better than the scoreline.
hints: Process outran scoreboard: margin rank #43 (margin +31) but SEI #15.
Defense drives the gap: SEI off #10 vs def #41.
SP+ halves: off #35, def #74.
Strongest metrics: RZ TD% +1.72, 2nd PPA +1.71, RZ TD% +1.57.
Weakest metrics: Pen yd -1.72, Fum% -1.62.

teams.explanation: 4-0 and +70 keeps SP+ at #11, but the plays say the wins were closer than the record: Houston by 2, Oregon State by 11. Our offense half sits at #59 — the Red Raiders move the ball at a league-average pace and the margin is carried by takeaways (INT% +2.38) rather than efficiency. Third-down PPA (+1.66) is the one offensive feature that pops. When the one-possession games bounce the other way, this profile is a .500 profile.
hints: Scoreboard outran process: margin rank #17 (margin +70) but SEI #33.
Offense drives the gap: SEI off #59 vs def #22.
SP+ halves: off #11, def #17.
Strongest metrics: INT% +2.38, 3rd PPA +1.66.

teams.explanation: SP+'s #25 tracks the +48 margin and the loss at Mississippi State. SEI is higher because the Tigers blow plays up on both sides — explosiveness +2.07 on offense, +1.65 allowed on defense — and first-down PPA (+1.59) says they move the ball early and often. The 45-17 shellacking of Florida is the profile talking; the 24-31 loss at Mississippi State is where it wasn't.
hints: Process outran scoreboard: margin rank #31 (margin +48) but SEI #8.
SP+ halves: off #40, def #14.
Strongest metrics: Exp +2.07, Exp +1.65, 1st PPA +1.59.

teams.explanation: SP+ loves the offense (#5); we rank the defense #45 and that is the whole gap. The Ducks' margin is +13 (#56) after the 31-39 loss at Oklahoma State, and their penalty rate is -2.20 — the worst discipline on the board. What is real: third-down PPA on both sides (+2.32 and +1.94) says Oregon wins the obvious downs. What is not: preventing anything between them, where the mirror features sit near average.
hints: Process outran scoreboard: margin rank #56 (margin +13) but SEI #22.
Defense drives the gap: SEI off #22 vs def #44.
SP+ halves: off #5, def #25.
Strongest metrics: 3rd PPA +2.32, 3rd PPA +1.94, INT% +1.82.
Weakest metrics: Pen -2.20.

teams.explanation: The only real argument on this list. SP+ has Georgia #1 overall and #1 on both halves; the +130 margin backs it. SEI's offense half agrees (#8, first-down PPA +2.26, TD% +1.74) but the defense half sits at #37 — the Bulldogs have allowed 17 to Arkansas and 14 to Vanderbilt, and their PPA-allowed and TD%-allowed numbers are only league-average. A margin model cannot see an untested defense; an efficiency model can only measure what was tested.
hints: Defense drives the gap: SEI off #9 vs def #38.
SP+ halves: off #1, def #1.
Strongest metrics: 1st PPA +2.26, 2nd PPA +1.77, TD% +1.74.

teams.explanation: SEI has Texas at #2 where SP+ stops at #7, and the difference is close-game luck, not process. Two of their four wins — 24-23 at Ohio State, 20-17 over Tennessee — came by a field goal or less, and SP+ discounts tight wins harder than we do. The plays are unambiguous: 2nd-down PPA +3.04 SD, drive TD% +2.63, red-zone TD% +2.17, and a defense that has allowed zero red-zone touchdowns all season. The schedule explains part of SP+'s caution, but the efficiency profile is what it is: an elite defense (#2) behind an offense that converts everything except its own penalties.
hints: Process outran scoreboard: margin rank #13 (margin +80) but SEI #2.
SP+ halves: off #16, def #5.
Strongest metrics: 2nd PPA +3.04, TD% +2.63, RZ TD% +2.17.
2 of 4 games decided by <=7 pts (SP+ penalizes close wins harder than SEI does).

teams.explanation: The defense is the board-seller: havoc +3.48 SD — off the chart — second-down PPA allowed +2.62, red-zone defense +2.62. That defense put 51 on Clemson and held Texas A&M to 6. SP+ sits at #10 because the offense's #22 half and the 24-32 loss at Ole Miss pull the margin down. We weight what the pass rush does to opposing drives more than one bad Saturday in Oxford.
hints: SP+ halves: off #22, def #4.
Strongest metrics: Havoc +3.48, RZ TD% +2.62, 2nd PPA +2.62.
